## Summary

- The Console adds an MCP module with a Metadata endpoint and an Entity endpoint. Each detail page shows the public path and a secret-free client template. A typed personal access token is checked against the signed-in user before any call. Discovery and a read run only when the user asks. A Metadata write is sent only after confirmation of that endpoint, user, tool, and argument snapshot. Stopping the wait does not treat an unanswered write as a rollback.
- Entity MCP is a read-only Streamable HTTP host at `{origin}/mcp/entity`. Tools are `list_entities`, `describe_entity`, `list_dictionary_codes`, `get_row`, `query_rows`, `validate_sql`, and `run_sql`. Each requires `entity:data_read` and the caller's effective read grants. The host does not write Entity rows, change definitions, or read the Change Log. Those tools are not on the Metadata host.
- Every Metadata and Entity catalog tool includes `execution` `read` or `write`. `tools/list` copies that value to `_meta["io.refraq/execution"]`. The Metadata writes are the semantics and join mutations. Every Entity tool is `read`, including `run_sql`.
- Change-log list and detail project the caller's current read grant. Continuation is an opaque `cursor` that expires in 60 seconds. Each side is `absent`, `visible`, or `unavailable`. The response names the logical version. It does not return `physical_table` or a raw stored image. No effective read grant is `404 ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`.
- Read Changes and Changes Dataset read as the platform System Identity and return those projected sides. `read.changes` with `shape` `net` fails with `CHANNEL_CHANGE_LOG_GROUPING_UNSAFE` when the declared Business Key is not a clear projected identity. Publish does not require those `entity_id` values to exist yet.
- Entity Data schema no longer returns `limits.offset_max`. `offset` is any integer greater than or equal to 0. A reference `target` is null unless the caller has an effective read grant on that Entity. When the shape withholds, get, query, and write rows include `__withheld`, and the array is empty when that row withholds nothing.
- `entity_query_timeout_sec` (default 30, range 5–300) and `entity_query_max_rows` (default 1000, range 100–10000) bound Entity MCP `run_sql`. They do not replace `query_timeout_sec` or `query_max_rows`.

## Operator notes

- Upgrade from v0.6.1. v0.1.6 and v0.1.9 were tagged and are not installable. Do not install them.
- Add `ENTITY_SIGNER_PASSWORD` to the live `.env` before starting this compose. Use URL-safe characters only (no `@`, `:`, `/`, `%`, `?`, or `#`), and keep it distinct from `ENTITY_OWNER_PASSWORD` and `ENTITY_READER_PASSWORD`. Compose interpolates it into `ENTITY_SIGNER_DATABASE_URL` for login `refraq_signer`. The process does not read the password name. `docker compose` refuses to start until the key is set. No other new key. Leave the rest of the live `.env` in place.
- Compose still mounts named volume `refraq_pg` at `/var/lib/postgresql`. Default PGDATA is `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`. A site already on that mount, including one upgraded through v0.1.10, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.6.0, or v0.6.1, keeps its cluster. A site that only used the published v0.1.8 asset must still copy the anonymous-volume cluster onto `refraq_pg` before `up -d`, using the command in the v0.1.10 notes. Do not run `docker compose down -v`. Do not restore `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
- Replace `docker-compose.yaml`, then `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. The new image tag recreates `ensure-entity-db` (`restart: "no"`). That one-shot still prepares `entity_data`, `entity_access`, `acl`, `channel_dataset`, and `entity_change_log`. It creates or aligns login `refraq_signer` (`LOGIN`, `NOSUPERUSER`, `NOBYPASSRLS`, `NOINHERIT`) and grants it execute only on `acl.ensure_signing_key()`. It installs `entity_access.profile_count` and `entity_access.profile_count_sql` beside the existing page functions. If role `refraq_channel_reader` is present, the same run revokes the privileges it holds in the entity database and drops the role. It does not delete Entity rows, change-log entries, or channel rows. api and worker still refuse to start while any of those five schemas is missing.
- The same api image adds service `entity-mcp` (`python -m backend.entity.mcp.http`, role `entity_mcp`). Compose does not publish its port. Web streams `{origin}/mcp/entity` to `http://entity-mcp:8002` with a 305-second proxy wait. The service opens the reader pool and the signer pool. It does not open the owner pool. Worker and Beat stay on the api image tag.
- API start runs Foundation Upgrade `0086_access_log_sql_fields`. It adds nullable `entity_access_logs.sql_sha256` and `entity_access_logs.statement_summary`. Existing rows stay null. A later `run_sql` writes those fields on the access-log row for verb `sql`. The upgrade does not delete tokens, catalog rows, Entity rows, channel rows, run records, or access-log rows. API start seeds `entity_query_timeout_sec` and `entity_query_max_rows` when the keys are missing. A value already stored is left as stored.
- `GET` and detail of `/entities/{id}/change-log` no longer accept `before_sequence` and no longer return `next_before_sequence`, envelope `row_id`, envelope `business_key`, or `physical_table`. Send `cursor` from `next_cursor`. The cursor is bound to the caller, the Entity, and the query, and it expires in 60 seconds. A blank, tampered, expired, or rebound cursor is `422 REQUEST_INVALID`. `row_identity` matches a clear projected Business Key. `version_id` and `row_id` are sent together. A lookup the list cannot answer is `422 ENTITY_CHANGE_LOG_QUERY_UNSUPPORTED`. An ineligible event and a missing sequence are `404 ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`. `entity:write` and `entity:access_manage` do not make an event readable. Stored change-log rows are not rewritten.
- Entity Data `schema` omits `limits.offset_max`. An `offset` above 10000 is no longer rejected for that cap. A large offset may return `504 PLATFORM_TIMEOUT`. A reference `target` is null when the caller has no effective read grant on the target Entity. Access preview still names that target. When `withheld_field` is `"__withheld"`, get, query, and write rows include the key, including an empty array.
- New `read.changes` and `volume.changes_dataset` executions store the projected sides. An execution already stored is returned as stored. `GET` of that output under `channel:read` does not apply the viewer's Entity policy. `CHANNEL_CHANGE_LOG_GROUPING_UNSAFE` proposes nothing. A graph can publish while those nodes' `entity_id` does not exist; the node fails at execution with `CHANNEL_NODE_FAILED` if it still does not resolve.
- Metadata MCP tool arguments and tool-call results are unchanged. `GET /mcp/catalog` and `tools/list` add `execution`. Webhook delivery is unchanged. Clients connect to Entity MCP with a User PAT at `{origin}/mcp/entity`. A Session cookie is not a credential on that path. Without `entity:data_read`, the tool list is empty, and a direct call is `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`. `run_sql` cancel is `ENTITY_SQL_TIMEOUT` (504). It is not `PLATFORM_TIMEOUT` and not `QUERY_TIMEOUT`. `ENTITY_SQL_FAILED` carries the SQLSTATE in its message.
- Rolling back to an older compose after this migration is not supported. Downgrade of `0086` drops `sql_sha256` and `statement_summary`.
